note: Rowlatt Act and satyagraha: 1919 (jess302, lehs303).
Chauri Chaura (Feb 1922) led Gandhi to withdraw the movement.
13 April 1919 (all four books).
Moplah (Malabar) rebellion of 1921 is not in hees202, hess208, jess302, lehs303 or the WBBSE Class VIII pages searched. Not in the NCERT/WBBSE books used.
Chauri Chaura incident.
1919, Amritsar.
AITUC's first president is not in the NCERT/WBBSE books used (labour history; not in NCERT).

DOUBTFUL KEY. 'First leader arrested in the non-cooperation movement' is not in any of the books used, so the official key (C. R. Das) can neither be confirmed nor contradicted. WBBSE only says Subhas Bose went to jail for activity in the movement; NCERT says thousands were jailed and Gandhi was arrested in March 1922. Not in NCERT.

NCERT hees202 says only that Tilak died in August 1920 (before the Nagpur session of Dec 1920); the exact day is not in any book used, so a student cannot match it to 'the day the movement was launched'. Chapter flags this in an exam_note.
Withdrawn February 1922.
Rowlatt Act and the 6 April hartal came before the 13 April massacre; chapter gives the sequence.
The nickname 'Black Bill' for the Rowlatt Act is in none of the books used (hess208 says Gandhi, Jinnah and others called it 'devilish' and tyrannical). Rowlatt Act itself is taught.
Muhammad Ali and Shaukat Ali (Ali brothers), with Azad, launched it (hees202). WBBSE instead says 'some Muslim League leaders'; exam_note covers it.
Amritsar.

Official key: Non-cooperation. Taught with an exam_note: hess208 calls the Rowlatt Satyagraha the first all-India struggle (largely urban), while jess302 says Gandhi then wanted a more broad-based movement, which was Non-Cooperation. Key stays authoritative.
Tolstoy's influence on Gandhi is not in the NCERT/WBBSE books used. Not in NCERT.
Charkha/khadi as symbol (lehs303, hees202).

Alluri Sitaram Raju led the Gudem Hills guerrilla movement of the early 1920s, arrested May 1924 ending a two-year armed struggle (jess302). The name 'Rampa' is not used in NCERT, so this is answerable only by recognising the leader.
'An eye for an eye...' quotation is not in the books used. Not in NCERT.
Eka movement is not named in the books used; only the Awadh peasant movement under Baba Ramchandra is taught. Not in NCERT.
Turkey (Ottoman Sultan-Caliph).
Hind Swaraj (1909) by Gandhi (jess302; WBBSE too).
Churchill's 'seditious fakir' remark (1931) is not in NCERT; belongs to HIS-25.
Navjivan is not named in the books used (Young India appears only as a source label in lehs303). Not in NCERT.
Gorakhpur (jess302, WBBSE).
Nagpur session, December 1920.
Rowlatt Act gave enormous powers to repress political activities (jess302).
Ehrar (Ahrar) League is not in the books used. Not in NCERT.
Tagore's objection to burning foreign cloth is not in NCERT or the WBBSE pages searched. WBBSE quotes his essay 'Swarajsadhan' criticising the charkha cult; chapter teaches that as a deep note only.
Who drafted the Congress inquiry report is not in the books used. Not in NCERT.
Madari Pasi / Eka movement not in the books used. Not in NCERT.
DOUBTFUL KEY. Congress Democratic Party is not in the books used; official key (Tilak) cannot be checked. Not in NCERT.

The Hunter Committee is not named in the books used: hees202 says only that a 'British-dominated inquiry committee' condemned Dyer. The chapter teaches the inquiry but not the name; the Jallianwala link is therefore not answerable from the text alone.
'Gandhi versus Lenin' by S. A. Dange is not in NCERT.
Tana Bhagat movement is not in the books used. Not in NCERT.
The full title 'Anarchical and Revolutionary Crimes Act' is in none of the books used; WBBSE says the Rowlatt bills aimed to stop the revolutionary movement, which supports but does not name it.
Chamber of Princes (1920) is not in NCERT; belongs to the constitutional chapter (HIS-27).
Congress delegation to Versailles (1919) is not in the books used. Not in NCERT.
Tagore renounced his knighthood in protest at the 1919 massacre. The books give no separate year for the renunciation; 1919 follows from the event.
South Africa.
Official key 1919-1922 matches hees202's timeline ('1919-1922: Khilafat Movement'); lehs303 labels it (1919-1920). exam_note gives both.
